sections.h2: Ways to sell a Perrysburg house fast
sections.html:
An owner here can hire a broker, market the property alone, or sell to a cash buyer who absorbs the repair bill. Perrysburg lies in Wood County, so deeds, tax bills and building permits involve county offices as well as city hall. Know who handles each task and the sale is less likely to stall at the finish.

  • A broker listing fits a house that can pass a lender's appraisal and survive weeks of showings.
  • Selling alone works when a closing agent or a lawyer drafts the deed and the settlement sheet.
  • A cash sale fits estate houses, occupied rentals and homes with a long repair list.

Perrysburg is a Wood County city on the south bank of the Maumee River, about 12 miles southwest of Toledo. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $329,700 and the median household earns $111,643. Just under two thirds of homes are lived in by their owners, so a sizeable share of the housing is rented. The city counted 20,623 residents in 2010 and has added roughly 4,800 since, which keeps demand steady for houses in good shape.

Both levels of government are involved. The City of Perrysburg grants zoning permits, and it contracts with Wood County Building Inspection for building permits, with the zoning permit coming first. The Planning and Zoning Division enforces codified ordinance Chapters 1210 through 1460 and also handles code enforcement, Board of Zoning Appeals applications and Historic Landmarks Commission cases.

A few of the division's answers help a seller who is closing out old projects:

  • Any change in a fence's height, style or location needs a permit.
  • Each new shed needs one, including a freestanding unit not fixed to the ground, and it must sit at least 5 feet off the lot line and 10 feet from the house.
  • Trailers and recreational vehicles may stay in a front or side yard between April 1 and October 31, on a hard surface at least 5 feet from any lot line.
  • City staff do not survey lots, so use a certified surveyor to find boundaries.

Zoning questions go to the office at 201 W Indiana Avenue, phone 419-872-8060. Building permit questions go to Wood County Building Inspection at 419-354-9190 on weekdays between 7:30 and 3:30, or toll free at 866-860-4140.

sections.h2: Rental owners and city income tax
sections.html: Landlords carry an extra obligation. Rental owners in Perrysburg must file a net profit income tax return on rental income and report tenants who move in or out. If you are selling a house that was rented, make sure those filings are current before closing, and tell the buyer which tenants are in place. Reporting each move-in and move-out as it happens keeps the city file accurate, and an accurate file is one less thing for a buyer's agent to question.

After closing, the deed goes to the Wood County Auditor before it reaches the recorder. Under Ohio Revised Code 322.02, any county transfer tax is paid by the grantor to the auditor when the deed is delivered, ahead of recording, and section 319.202 requires a statement of value to be submitted. The auditor answers at 419-354-9150 or 866-860-4140. Your closing agent or lawyer normally handles the filing, but it helps to know the office exists if a document is sent back.

The Wood County Treasurer collects real estate tax in two installments, due in February and July. About eighty taxing districts exist in the county, each with its own rate, so a Perrysburg bill reflects the levies at that address. Payments go by mail to the treasurer at 1 Courthouse Square in Bowling Green or to participating banks, several with Perrysburg branches, until close of business on the due date, and mailed payments must be postmarked by then. After the due date a 5 percent penalty applies for the first 10 days, rising to 10 percent after that, as Ohio Revised Code 323.13 sets out.

At closing the settlement sheet divides the current bill between you and the buyer, so ask the treasurer's office which installment is paid and which is still owed.

Section 5302.30 of the Ohio code tells you to hand buyers the state form promptly. It asks about the water supply, the sewer system, the roof and foundation, and defects you know of. Fiduciary transfers from an estate and inherited houses that you did not occupy in the past year are exempt. Fill the form out with care, and attach any permit records you have for fences, sheds or other work.

sections.h2: Order of steps for a Perrysburg closing
sections.html:
Most delays come from sequence, not from any single office. Begin by pulling your permit history: ask Planning and Zoning about fences, sheds and any parked trailer, then ask Wood County Building Inspection whether any building permit is still open. Next, decide on the route, broker, solo sale or cash offer. Once a buyer is lined up, deliver the disclosure form, let your closing agent or lawyer draft the deed and settlement sheet, and confirm with the treasurer which tax installment is paid.

On closing day the deed is signed and delivered, the county transfer tax if any is paid through the auditor before recording, and the tax bill is divided. If the house was rented, the city income tax filing and the tenant report should already be done. Keep copies of the signed deed, the settlement sheet and the disclosure form for your own records.

sections.h2: When a cash purchase suits a Perrysburg owner
sections.html:
A cash buyer is worth considering when speed or condition matters more than top price: an inherited house nobody plans to fix up, a rental with tenants inside, or a job move on a short clock. The house sells with its flaws, which spares you contractors, showings and waiting on an appraisal.

Request the offer in writing and weigh it against a listing's likely result after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Learn who pays the transfer charges, which day closes the sale, and what happens if the buyer discovers a defect. Declining an offer does not stop you from listing.

faqs.q: Who issues a building permit for a Perrysburg house?
faqs.a: Wood County Building Inspection, after the City of Perrysburg has issued a zoning permit. The zoning permit must be obtained before the building permit is released.

faqs.q: Does swapping out a fence in Perrysburg need a permit?
faqs.a: A permit is required any time a fence changes in height, style or location. For a replacement identical in height, style and position, confirm with Planning and Zoning at 419-872-8060 before starting.

faqs.q: When do Wood County tax bills come due?
faqs.a: In February and July each year. Pay late and a 5 percent penalty applies during the first 10 days, then 10 percent.

faqs.q: Do Perrysburg landlords owe city income tax on rent?
faqs.a: Yes. The city asks owners of rental property to file a net profit income tax return for rental income and to report tenants who occupy or leave their units.

faqs.q: Which disclosures apply when I sell a Perrysburg home?
faqs.a: The state form under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 applies, covering the water supply, sewer system, structure, hazardous materials and known defects, delivered to buyers promptly.
